title: Man killed by police was a kind person, says his mother
article: The mother of a young man shot and killed by Port Moody police earlier this week said he was a kind and sensitive person who probably felt threatened by the officer.
"He was a young man, with lots of talent and a bright future for him," said Farough Jabalamei in an interview with CTV last night.

Keyvan Tabesh, 18, was shot early Monday when he allegedly lunged at the plainclothes officer with a machete. Earlier that night, two women had told police that a group of young men bumped their car from behind, and that one man jumped out of the car and smashed in their back window with a machete.

The men fled the scene, but a plainclothes officer spotted the car and followed it into a cul-de-sac, where the shootings occurred. Another man was also shot, but he survived. He has told police that they didn't know the man was a police officer.

Tabesh, who was working at an auto-body shop and had talked about starting his own business, came here from Iran two years ago. But his mom said Tabesh felt unsafe here and was often teased by students at his new school.
Jabalamei said her son started to carry a knife after he was stabbed in the face by another young man.
Jabalamei added that her son worried he could be attacked again at any time.
Const. Brian Soles said witness accounts of the incident support the police version, in which Tabesh was running at the officer with an upraised machete.
Although Tabesh was prohibited from driving, that night he was behind the wheel of his Honda Prelude with two male friends from Coquitlam.
